report.headline: EuroLeague playmaker projected toward a near-league-average NBA usage role, but the shooting efficiency projection carries no signal

projection.text: Usage rate is projected at 19.9% in the NBA, essentially matching the league's minutes-weighted average of 20.1%, with an 80% prediction interval of 14.7% to 25.0% — a span that covers nearly the full width of a single standard deviation of NBA usage (5.2%) on either side.

risks.text: Turnover rate was elevated at 18.6% in the source season.

True shooting was already below the EuroLeague average (53.7%, -0.55 sd), and the raw NBA projection of 52.9% sits further below the target league's 55.7% average — though this specific projection is not reliable given the model's performance on this metric.

The 80% prediction interval for usage rate (14.7% to 25.0%) spans almost two full standard deviations of NBA usage variation, so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot pin down an individual value.

The estimate rests on 61 historical EL->NBA transitions among players who, conditional on making the move, already sat +0.46 sd above their own league's average — a moderate cohort size that limits precision.

strengths.text: Posted a 32.5% assist rate and 7.058 assists per 75 possessions in the EuroLeague, indicating a heavy playmaking role.
Carried a EuroLeague usage rate of 24.4%, about +0.96 standard deviations above that league's average, showing a significant offensive role before the move.
Scored 16.268 points per 75 possessions with a shot profile leaning heavily on threes (41.4% of attempts).

uncertainty.text: The true shooting projection of 52.9% should not be treated as informative: the model's out-of-fold error on this metric (4.5%) is larger than the error from simply guessing the league average (4.3%), meaning it loses to a trivial baseline.
